bc_goldfinger.blurb: Goldfinger is a boulder sector in the Hunter Creek forest near Hope in the Fraser Valley, and it is the first group of boulders you meet on the walk in. It holds 14 problems that split into two camps: a handful of easy to moderate lines from the bottom of the scale up to about V3, and a harder group from V8 to V11 with nothing much in between. The setting is open forest with uneven ground, so bring pads and a spotter. It works as a quick warm-up stop or a short after-work session, and it sits right beside a smaller neighbouring boulder with its own classic.
bc_goldfinger.parking_note: Leave the car at the upper parking area along the forest service road; the sector is a very short walk east from there.
bc_goldfinger.approach: From the upper parking area walk east up the forest road for under 100 m. The boulders are on your left, and a short trail drops down to the forest floor at the base of the main boulder.

bc_marble_canyon_ice.blurb: Marble Canyon Ice is a winter venue in the Cariboo region of south-central British Columbia, in a limestone canyon on the Lillooet and Cache Creek side of Highway 99. It is a long day trip from Vancouver. The 14 climbs are mostly mixed lines, with M grades running from the mid-range up to M9, plus a few ice routes that range from WI2 to WI6. Several lines can be top-roped, which is unusual for ice on the west coast, so the main wall can draw a crowd on winter weekends. A short walk gets you to the base, and the top of the ice is visible from the lake edge.

bc_helheim.blurb: Helheim is a small sport crag in the Slocan Valley of the West Kootenays, tucked below the dirt road that leads toward the Gimli and Valhalla area. It holds 14 routes, mostly bolted sport lines plus a couple of top-rope problems, with grades concentrated in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, one at 5.9 and one at 5.13. The walls are steep and feature-rich, which suits climbers who like short, sustained pitches. It is a handy back-up objective when the higher peaks are rained out, though it is a modest crag rather than a full-day destination.

bc_shinobi_gardens.blurb: Shinobi Gardens is a bouldering area in the Silver Lake basin of the Fraser Valley, in the Hope area. It has 14 problems and leans hard: only one problem is in the V2 range, a few are around V4 and V5, and the rest climb from V7 up to the V11-12 range. That makes it more of a destination for stronger boulderers than for beginners, although a couple of lower lines are there for warming up. Several problems share start holds on the same boulder, so plan the day around a few blocks and bring pads.
